title: DNWP0016 - WAGR Enabling Works and Strip-out - Sellafield - A2R JV
description: WAGR Overview and Site Information The Windscale Advanced Gas-cooled Reactor (WAGR), commissioned in 1962, was the prototype for the UK's second-generation Advanced Gas-cooled Reactor (AGR) fleet. The facility (Building B50), recognised by its distinctive spherical containment shell, was supported by the fuel assembly building (B52) and turbine hall (B55). Following reactor core dismantling and removal in 2012, the WAGR Complex entered Care and Maintenance (C&M). The facility is now progressing towards its final phase of decommissioning and demolition. Existing records confirm the presence of Low-Level Waste (LLW) and Intermediate-Level Waste (ILW), resulting in ongoing radiological and contamination hazards. All buildings within the WAGR area are owned by the Remediation operating unit, remain under active surveillance and maintenance, and are classified as Beta Gamma contamination facilities. Project Scope The scope comprises enabling, strip-out, waste management and decommissioning support activities across the WAGR facility, alongside support for wider Windscale decommissioning programmes and emergent operational requirements. Key activities include (see attachment) - Strip-out Works: Internal and external removal of fixtures, fittings, equipment and non-structural elements to facilitate future decommissioning and demolition activities. - Radiological Waste Management: Safe handling, removal and management of LLW and ILW in accordance with site requirements. - Asset Reinstatement: Delivery of asset reinstatement works and provision of SQEP resources to support successful handover. - Pre-Construction Information (PCI): Support information gathering and site characterisation where existing PCI is insufficient. - Surveys: Plan and undertake surveys to assess radiological, hazardous and operational conditions in support of future decommissioning works. - Project Enabling Works: Design, fabricate, trial and implement enabling solutions, equipment and materials to support project delivery. - Asbestos Management: Planning, sampling, monitoring and licensed asbestos removal where required. - Procurement: Procurement of materials, equipment and associated quality documentation. - Waste Management: Sorting, segregation, consolidation and disposal of current and historical wastes, including completion of documentation for transfer to Sellafield Waste Coordinators. - Emergent Works: Rapid response support to operations and maintenance teams for safety-critical issues. - Temporary Works: Management, design and construction of temporary works, including scaffolding, enclosures and other supporting structures. - Decontamination: Decontamination activities to support area declassification and radiological rollback. - Plant Modifications: Production of Plant Modification Proposals (PMPs) and associated documentation. - Scaffolding Services: Provision of scaffolding design, supply and installation resources as required. Additional information: https://www.linkedin.com/company/a2r-altrad-atkinsrealis-remediation https://www.gov.uk/government/news/sellafield-ltd-awards-high-hazard-risk-reduction-framework-contract

Simply responding capability by emailing or responding to this notice with your contact information that you are interested/capable is encouraged. No capability statement is required. title: Construction IDIQ Contract, FLETC Charleston, SC
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. Project Title: Construction IDIQ Contract, FLETC Charleston, SC Solicitation Number: 70LCHS26RPFB00001 NOTICE: Interested vendors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments (if applicable). The solicitation is anticipated to be posted within 2-4 weeks, with proposal due approximately 30 calendar days after issuance. A site visit will be conducted, and vendors must respond promptly to allow sufficient time for base access processing. Site visit details and access instructions will be provided in the solicitation. The Government intends to award one (1) firm-fixed price Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for construction, additions, alterations, maintenance, and repairs at buildings and structures located at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) in Charleston, South Carolina. Work will be performed through the issuance of individual task orders issued under the contract. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision, and quality control necessary to perform the work specified in the basic contract and individual task orders. The contract will include a 12-month base period, four 12-month option periods, and an optional six-month extension in accordance with FAR 52.217-8. The contract minimum guarantee is $50,000 and the maximum value is not-to-exceed $33,000,000.00 over the contract's life. For planning purposes only, the Government estimates approximately $6,000,000.00 in task orders annually; this amount is not guaranteed nor is the Government limited by this amount annually. Individual task orders are anticipated to range from approximately $2,000 to $1,500,000.00. Task orders may encompass multiple construction trades, including but not limited to architectural, mechanical, civil, structural, roofing, demolition, electrical, environmental support, carpentry, roadwork, painting, plumbing, and masonry. Task order pricing will be based on the most current R.S. Means Facility Construction Cost Data Book, adjusted using the Charleston, South Carolina, City Cost Index multiplier. The contractor's coefficient will be applied to the total adjusted bare costs for labor, materials, and equipment. This acquisition is set aside for HUBZone small business concerns. FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, will apply. The applicable limitations require the contractor to perform at least 15 percent (15%) of the cost of the contract, not including the cost of materials, with its own employees. The Government is anticipating significant subcontracting opportunities under this contract.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation, quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation is being issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 dated 13 Mar 2026. This solicitation number W91ZRS27QA001 is for the Connecticut Army National Guard (CTARNG). The USPFO for Connecticut intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price contract for CMT Catered Meals. This request is due by 03 November 2026 at 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time). This solicitation is 100% small business set aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 311991 � (Perishable Prepared Food Manufacturing). The small business standard size for NAICS 311991 is 700 employees. Instructions to Offerors All questions shall be in writing. Questions may be faxed to Leslie Fedler at 860-386-4070 or emailed at leslie.a.fedler.civ@army.mil. Questions must be submitted No Later Than 30 October 2026. All quotes are due no later than 1:00 p.m. eastern time, 03 November 2026. Quotes may be faxed to Leslie Fedler at 860-386-4070 or emailed to leslie.a.fedler.civ@army.mil. It is your responsibility to make sure your quote is received. The fact that the contracting office did not receive your quote due to an error on the fax machine or email address does not change the due date or time. Basis for Award "The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Award will be made on an 'all or none' basis to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offeror. Tradeoffs will not be permitted. Quotes will be evaluated for technical acceptability, past performance acceptability, and price." Evaluation Process: "The Government intends to evaluate quotes by first sorting them from lowest price to highest price. The lowest-priced quote will then be evaluated for technical acceptability and past performance. If the lowest-priced quote is determined to be 'Technically Acceptable' and has 'Acceptable Past Performance,' award will be made to that offeror, and no further quotes will be evaluated." Factor 1: Technical Acceptability: "The technical quote will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis. To be rated Acceptable, the quote must clearly demonstrate a compliance approach that meets all requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS), specifically demonstrating the capability to distribute media across the required channels and networks." Factor 2: Past Performance: "Past Performance will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. To be rated Acceptable, the offeror must submit a minimum of two (2) references within the past three (3) years demonstrating similar scope, complexity, and NAICS 311991 relevance. Offerors with no relevant past performance history will receive a 'Neutral' rating, which will be treated as 'Acceptable' for award purposes." Factor 3: Price: "Price will be evaluated for mathematical completeness and price reasonableness. Award will be made to the lowest total priced, responsible offeror whose technical and past performance quotes are rated Acceptable." The Contracting Officer is not responsible for locating or obtaining any information not identified in the offer. The Government is not responsible for developing the comparison from insufficient information provided. description: Amendment 04 is attached to provide the answers to Industry's questions regarding this RFI. Attachment 2-RFI_M67854-26-I-4208_Official_QA_20261021_Public Release is provided in the attachments. No further extension will be provided beyond 03 November 2026. Amendment 03 is attached to revise the response due date from 19 October 2026 at 1:00 P.M. to 03 November 2026 at 1:00 P.M. Questions and answers are in final review and will be released in Amendment 04. Please see below for Market Research Clarifications. Market Research Clarification Statements: 1. Clarification on Primary Scope and Contractor-Provided Tooling: The Government reiterates that the primary requirement of this effort is the provision of skilled, professional IT touch-labor services (Objective 1). Any proposed AI/automation tooling must be presented as an embedded component of the service delivery model, consistent with the constraints in Section 3.2 of the RFI, designed to augment the workforce and improve efficiency. 2. Additional Request for Information on Service-Based Ordering Models: In addition to the areas outlined in the original RFI, the Government is seeking industry feedback on recommended ordering approaches for service-based delivery models. Respondents are encouraged to describe frameworks where the Government could procure "hours of service" or service outcomes rather than individual labor categories. Descriptions should include associated tooling considerations, structural elements that support efficient ordering, and methods for performance tracking. 3. Clarification on Submission Formatting: To resolve confusion identified in industry questions, respondents are instructed to adhere to the following: The "Capabilities Narrative" is limited to five (5) pages (PDF). Any optional "Supplementary Materials" are separate and limited to fifteen (15) pages (PDF). The "Vendor Comment Matrix" must be submitted in its native Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) format, and the 300-word limit per cell is in effect. 4. Clarification on ROM Pricing and Software Licensing: To resolve the conflict identified between RFI Section 3.2 and Area B, respondents are instructed that this is a services acquisition. Any costs associated with contractor-provided proprietary tooling (licensing, subscriptions, etc.) are expected to be included within the fully burdened labor rates of the "Labor" ROM component. The "Platform Licensing/Subscription" and "Variable/Consumption Costs" line items should be used only for estimating potential Government-incurred costs on Government-owned platforms (e.g., ServiceNow credits, Power Platform licensing). If a vendor's solution does not generate such costs, those line items should be marked as $0. Amendment 02 is attached to revise the response due date from 5 October 2026 at 1:00 P.M. to 19 October 2026 at 1:00 P.M. Questions are in the process of being answered. No additional questions will be accepted at this time. Amendment 01 is attached to revise the release date and the response due date. Thank you! The Marine Corps Systems Command (MARCORSYSCOM), Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS), is conducting market research to identify capable, innovative commercial partners to deliver comprehensive, enterprise-scale Information Technology (IT) Operational Support Services (OSS). While providing qualified, certified personnel remains the primary focus, the Government is simultaneously exploring the integration of commercial AI and automation technologies as a critical capability for our selected partner(s) to drive operational efficiencies. Consolidating professional services represents a strategic opportunity to optimize workflows and lower manual touch-labor costs over time by equipping the contractor workforce with advanced automation tools.

description: Notice Type: Sources Sought Notice Solicitation No.: 75N98027SS00013 Posted Date: October 19, 2026 Response Date: November 3, 2026 Response Time: 1:00 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) NAICS Code: 315990 Apparel Accessories and Other Apparel manufacturing, with 500 in size standards in number of employees. Product Service Code: 8415 Clothing, Special Purpose Title: Sources Sought Specialized Disposable Gloves Disclaimer This is a Sources Sought Notice. This is not a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability of domestically manufactured products to meet the requirement described herein. This notice does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government as a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing a response. Agency/Office Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) National Institutes of Health (NIH) Office of Logistics and Acquisition Operations (OLAO) Description The HHS/NIH/OLAO is seeking to obtain information regarding the availability of U.S. manufactured specialized disposable gloves. The HHS personnel including clinicians, researchers, laboratory personnel, animal care staff, maintenance personnel, and other staff who may encounter chemical, biological, clinical, research, animal care, facility, diagnostic, or related workplace hazards require specialized disposable gloves to safely perform their duties of clinical, research, diagnostic, laboratory, animal care, maintenance, decontamination, cleaning, waste handling, facility-support, and emergency preparedness activities that support the Department's mission. These gloves are a critical element of personal protective equipment for personnel who handle or may respond to a national or international incident that would result I their contact with hazardous chemicals, biological materials, infectious or potentially infectious substances and diseases, contaminated surfaces, research specimens, animal-related materials, cleaning and disinfecting agents, and other materials presenting exposure risks. Gloves must be appropriate for the specific hazards, environments, and tasks for which they are used. Glove performance is evaluated on hazard-specific protective characteristics, including material, thickness, barrier integrity, chemical resistance, degradation resistance, permeation performance, durability, dexterity, fit, tactile sensitivity, puncture or tear resistance, and compatibility with the intended task. Chemical Applications - Gloves should be supported, where available, by product-specific chemical resistance documentation for the material and thickness being procured. Such documentation typically includes permeation testing (ASTM F739 or equivalent), which establishes how long a glove resists breakthrough by a given chemical, and degradation testing (ASTM D471, ANSI/ISEA 105, or equivalent), which establishes whether the glove material physically deteriorates on contact. description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Title: University Centers for Excellence in Developmental Disabilities Education, Research and Service Community Impact and Capacity Building Initiative: Technical Assistance to Strengthen Outcomes for People with I/DD and Their Families Issuing Office: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Administration for Community Living (ACL), Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), on behalf of the Administration on Disabilities (AoD) NAICS Code: For purposes of this market research, the Government anticipates that NAICS Code 541611 � Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services may best represent the principal purpose of the contemplated requirement. This designation is preliminary and may be revised as a result of market research. Respondents who believe another NAICS code more appropriately reflects the principal purpose of the contemplated requirement should identify the recommended NAICS code and briefly explain the basis for that recommendation. PURPOSE OF THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes in accordance with RFO FAR 15.101(c). The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. Responses to this RFI will be treated as information only and not as proposals. Responses are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The issuance of this RFI does not constitute a solicitation, a promise to issue a solicitation, or an obligation on the part of the Government to procure any products or services. The purpose of this RFI is to: Gather information from industry regarding the general approach, feasibility, staffing models, and anticipated cost of performing the type of work described in the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS); Obtain industry recommendations regarding potential prioritization, phasing, scaling, or restructuring of the contemplated work; Assess the relationship between the contemplated scope, anticipated resource requirements, and likely market pricing; and Inform ACL/AoD's decisions regarding scope, task structure, phasing, and acquisition strategy as the PWS is finalized. The draft PWS provided with this RFI is for market research purposes only and remains subject to revision. Respondents should not assume that the final scope, task structure, deliverables, or performance standards in the PWS will appear in any resulting solicitation. The Government is specifically interested in industry feedback that identifies where the described scope may be too broad, too narrow, under-resourced, or structured in a way that drives unnecessary cost, so that the requirement can be refined prior to release of a solicitation. BACKGROUND The Administration on Disabilities (AoD), within ACL/HHS, is responsible for administering the Developmental Disabilities Assistance and Bill of Rights Act of 2000 (DD Act), which establishes the National Network of University Centers for Excellence in Developmental Disabilities Education, Research, and Service (UCEDDs). AoD is considering a contract vehicle to provide network-wide training, technical assistance (TA), and capacity-building support to UCEDD. Through this RFI, the Government seeks industry feedback concerning the feasibility, resource requirements, potential cost drivers, and appropriate structure of the contemplated requirement. The Government is also interested in identifying opportunities to prioritize, phase, scale, or otherwise structure the work to achieve program objectives efficiently. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDENTS Interested parties are requested to submit a written response of no more than seven (7) pages, excluding the cover page. Please include in your response: Company name, address, point of contact, phone, email, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), if the respondent elects to provide it; Business size, applicable socioeconomic status (small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) and applicable NAICS code(s) under which your firm is classified; Provide a brief description of the organization�s capabilities and relevant experience performing comparable technical assistance, capacity-building, evaluation, knowledge management, or technology support contracts, particularly any involving disability networks, university-based centers, HHS/ACL, or similarly structured federal TA contracts; and Responses to the questions below. RFI QUESTIONS Respondents are encouraged to provide concise, specific information directly responsive to the questions below. Marketing materials or general corporate information that does not address the contemplated requirement are not necessary. Interested and capable organizations are requested to address the following questions: Based on the draft PWS, describe whether the contemplated scope appears feasible and identify any tasks, deliverables, performance requirements, or assumptions that may create significant performance, staffing, schedule or cost risk. Identify any areas of the draft requirement that industry recommends clarifying, restructuring, consolidating, or otherwise revising; Describe the general staffing model and categories of labor or expertise that would reasonably be required to perform the contemplated work. Identify any specialized expertise, staffing assumptions, or other resources that would materially affect performance or cost; Provide a rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimate of annual cost to perform the general scope described in the PWS, and the basis for that estimate. The ROM is requested solely for acquisition planning and market research purposes. Please identify the significant assumptions and primary cost drivers underlying the estimate; Provide recommendations on which elements of the contemplated scope should be prioritized, phased, scaled, or consolidated to achieve the greatest programmatic value without materially affecting the overall objectives of the requirement. Respondents may recommend alternative approaches or scope adjustments that could improve efficiency, reduce cost, or enhance the likelihood of successful performance; Based on the technology related functions contemplated in the draft PWS, describe, the technology approach your organization would propose for supporting the Core Functions Dashboard and AI-assisted chatbot (e.g., existing commercial/Government-authorized platforms vs. custom development), including anticipated cost drivers, timeline, and relevant privacy/security/accessibility (Section 508) considerations; and Based on the nature of the contemplated services, identify and recommendations regarding acquisition structure or contract type that the Government should consider. Respondents may address, as applicable: Fixed-price, cost-reimbursement, time-and-materials, labor-hour, or hybrid approaches; Use of a single contract or other acquisition structure; Task organization or phasing approaches; and Any acquisition structure that could reduce performance risk, administrative burden, or unnecessary cost. Recommendations should include a brief explanation of the underlying rationale. Submission Instructions: Responses must be submitted electronically to Khaled.Gohar@hhs.gov no later than November 03, 2026, 2:00 PM ET. Responses should reference RFI - UCEDD Technical Assistance in the subject line. Proprietary information must be clearly marked. Respondents should avoid including proprietary or confidential information unless it is necessary to meaningfully respond to the RFI. The Government may use information submitted in response to the RFI for market research and acquisition planning purposes, including refinement of the requirement and acquisition strategy. Disclaimer: This RFI is for information and planning purposes only a

title: SOURCES SOUGHT: COMMERCIAL AVAILABLILITY OF FULLY AUTOMATED CLEAN SHOP WET PROCESS SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED EQUIPMENT B794 NAS JAX, FL
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET SURVEY FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY, TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL COMMERCIAL AVAILABLILITY OF FULLY AUTOMATED CLEAN SHOP WET PROCESS SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED EQUIPMENT FOR THE DESIGN- BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, RENOVATION OF B794 CLEANING SHOP, AT NAVAL AIR STATION (NAS) JACKSONVILLE, FL THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The reference number for this posting is N6945027RB794. This is a market research tool being used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources that can manufacture and install a fully automated clean shop wet process system and associated equipment. Project Description: The procurement for B794 encompasses design, engineering and construction services, along with the integration of personal property and transition services necessary for the renovation of the Cleaning Shop, located within existing B794 at NAS Jacksonville, FL. New equipment will be integrated and work cohesively as a system. Each cleaning line in the system must be equipped with two bridge-crane-style material transporters that have enclosed canopy-style ventilation with three process lines, programmed to work together. The lines should be compact with less than 6� between each tank. The cleaning lines must have dedicated spray rinse tanks and manual spray cleaning booths that are incorporated into the line. Transporting the components for processing must be done in 3-axis: Vertical (Lifting), Horizontal (Lateral), and Horizontal (Longitudinal). The automated cleaning line shall be a comprehensive system designed to clean aircraft components, record data, and report errors to operators of the system. The unit must operate in limited production space and requires control integration to properly process the needed production. The contractor must demonstrate experience with this specific type of cleaning lines: compact (width restrictions with tanks being less than 6� apart; ventilation hoods cannot be used with space constraints), fully automated, with canopy style hood ventilation on the material transporter with hard ducting. The cleaning system must work as a unit and be controlled from its own Human Machine Interface (HMI) or a central master supervisory HMI/SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) station that coordinates automated material transporters and line handoffs across all three lines. Integrated systems are: Heavy-duty cleaning lines Titanium cleaning line Vapor degreasers Associated support and ancillary process equipment The cleaning equipment must utilize a canopy-style hooded material transporter to eliminate the amount of exhaust air. This must reduce the energy consumption of the line to the required level while also improving environmental air emissions. The system must use ducting that does not flex and is not prone to heavy maintenance requirements or fatigue failures. To maintain consistency, quality, reliability, and deliverability, the equipment for the clean shop renovation should utilize products that have been designed and proven to work in the industry for over 5 years with experience that will allow integration of multiple cleaning products. For each project, provide the customer point of contact including name, phone number, and email, and a narrative description of the product/services provided by your organization. Also provide project title, project location (city/state), procurement contract number, and contract value, if available. Include the following information for automated cleaning systems: Model Number, Catalog Number, Code Number, or equivalent model designation Product Description Manufacturer's technical data sheets. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate experience in relation to the areas specified herein. title: P8-A Ground Station (PGS) Aircraft Media Gateway (AMG) Production, Installation and Sustainment Support
description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. REQUIREMENTS: Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) PMA-290 P-8A program office has a requirement for additional quantities of ground systems hardware and software in support of the P-8A I3B2 aircraft and legacy aircraft. This effort will provide continued modifications and installs of P-8A Ground Station (PGS) systems, and other support for Mobile Mission Systems to include Poseidon Quick Look (PQL) and Fly Away Kit (FAK). The contractor�s effort will also include associated support activities and other direct costs (ODCs). This action does not introduce new mission areas or fundamentally new capabilities. The requested information is to assist the Government in conducting market research to determine potential business sources that have the assets, skills, experience, financial stability, qualifications, and knowledge required to support the above request. Include a statement regarding industrial security clearance. This Sources Sought is not, however, a request for inquiries concerning subcontracting opportunities. AMG is integrated within P-8A Ground Stations (PGS) for media building purposes to support missions for P-8A Block I and Block II aircraft. The anticipated period of performance for this effort is Q2FY27 through Q1FY30. SUBMISSION DETAILS: Interested persons may submit a Capability Statement identifying their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. Only Capability Statements received on or before 15 calendar days after the posting date of this Notice will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this Notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability Statements received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Capability Statements submitted should be pertinent and specific in the technical/management/business area under consideration, on each of the following qualifications. Small/Large Business Status: A company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), DUNS Number, CAGE Code, and a statement regarding current small/large business status. Technical Data/ Computer Software Documentation: Since the Government does not possess sufficient technical data that a Contractor would require in order for that Contractor to fulfill the planned requirements, each interested party must demonstrate that its company currently possesses or has authorized access to the necessary technical data, computer software and computer software documentation, or has a viable plan to obtain, generate, or otherwise secure authorized access to the necessary technical data, computer software and computer software documentation; and that it will be maintained throughout the duration of the effort being solicited. Execution: A description of the technical approach for meeting the requirements of the contemplated procurements. If a small business, provide a description of the plan for ensuring that the small business performs at least 50% of the work itself in terms of cost of performance. Experience: A description of previous (awarded within last 3 years) or current relevant contracts. Personnel: Name, professional qualifications and specific experience of key personnel (e.g., program manager(s), project manager(s), technical lead(s), etc. Facilities: Availability and description of facilities and equipment that will be utilized to meet requirements. Security: A description of facility and personnel security regarding the handling and storage of classified information and hardware. The information submitted should address feasibility of performing the following task for integration with P-8A Ground Station (PGS): Description of the Contractor's approach in the sustainment of software and hardware of P-8A Ground Station (PGS) specifically for Aircraft Media Gateway (AMG) to support P-8A aircraft. Include specific relevant technical and management experience performed in the past five (5) years. Any other specific and pertinent information as pertains to this particular area of procurement that would enhance our consideration and evaluation of the Capability Statement. Interested parties are advised against submitting a Capability Statement that merely mimics information in this Notice, provides brochure-like information, or provides general information. Responses to this Notice are not to exceed 20 pages in length on 8.5 x 11-inch paper with one inch margins and font no smaller than 10 point Times New Roman. The Government requests that respondents deliver responses electronically via e-mail in Microsoft Word or PDF format with proper data markings for unclassified and proprietary information not later than 15 calendar days after the posting date of this Notice. Classified material SHALL NOT be submitted. All submissions shall include this Sources Sought Notice Reference Number, company name, company address, CAGE code, DUNS number, and a point-of-contact who is able to discuss the Capability Statement submitted. Point-of-contact information shall include name, position, phone number, and email address. Acknowledgement of receipt will be provided. All information submitted will be adequately safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure in accordance with FAR 15.207. All submissions must be clearly marked with the following caption: For Official Use Only, Releasable to Government Agencies for Evaluation Purposes Only. title: Barbados – Electrical power systems design services – Caribbean Electricity Integrator Facility
description: The Caribbean Electricity Integrator Facility (CEIF) will provide integrated technical, engineering and transaction-advisory support to advance priority electricity-integration investments in the Caribbean from analysis and project identification towards investment and tender readiness. The specific objective of the contract is to validate regional Caribbean electricity-interconnection options and prepare, through an integrator approach, a St Kitts and Nevis-anchored Northern Corridor package that can reach at least tender or contracting readiness where feasible, while developing a replicable mechanism for future Caribbean electricity-integration corridors. The initial focus will be on St Kitts and Nevis, including the interconnection between St Kitts and Nevis and the associated generation, grid and enabling infrastructure required to support a viable integrated electricity system. The assignment will also assess the potential extension of the Northern Corridor towards Antigua and Barbuda and other Northern Leeward receiving/readiness nodes, subject to technical, economic and commercial validation. The contractor will assess the relevant technical, economic, financial, legal, commercial, environmental, social, institutional and procurement dimensions and develop viable business, financing, risk-allocation and procurement structures for priority investments. The work will also support the development of a scale-up and replication mechanism for a wider pipeline of Caribbean electricity-integration investments. The direct beneficiaries and geographical focus will include Caribbean partner countries covered by the EU-Caribbean Cooperation Facility+ and, where relevant to the electricity-interconnection agenda, Caribbean Overseas Countries and Territories and French Outermost Regions, with the precise geographical scope of subsequent corridors to be determined through the analysis. The contractor will provide an engineering-anchored transaction advisory team, combining strong power-system, grid and submarine-interconnection capability with expertise in market and demand analysis, economics, financial structuring, legal and commercial design, procurement, environmental and social safeguards and stakeholder engagement.

title: 6505--Sacubitril/Valsartan Tablets (VA-27-00014055)
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The VA Enterprise Procurement Office intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) 36E79727R0007 for an unrestricted procurement for Sacubitril-Valsartan Tablets, for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) (inclusive of Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacies (CMOPs) and Option 2 State Veterans Homes (SVH)), Department of Defense (DoD) (inclusive of Tricare Mail Order Pharmacies (TMOPs)), Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Indian Health Service (IHS), and Federal Health Care Center (FHCC). VA will award one contract to the responsible offeror who will be able to provide an uninterrupted source of supply for the contracted items. The contract period will be for one year plus four pre-priced one-year option periods. The contract items will be distributed through the VA s and DOD s respective Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor Programs. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. Offerors must state the exact name (name that appears on label) by which the drug will be supplied and have an NDC number that is unique to the offeror. The successful offeror/contractor's label with its unique NDC shall be the only label on the product. Contractors shall not affix their label over another label on the product. VA labels must be able to securely adhere on top of the successful offeror/contractor s label. All unit of use packaging identified in the Schedule of Supplies, (60 & 180 count bottles) shall contain a safety-cap capable of having the outer part of the cap deshelled and / or a convertible cap to produce a non-safety cap and a bottle with a minimum required size of 120cc volume. The safety cap must not exceed the diameter of the bottle. The bottle must have a cylindrical body and minimum of 5.75 circumference. The bottle must fit a label with a dimension of 5.25 x 2 . The 0.5 additional space is required to keep the bar code exposed and/or allow for the display of the expiration date and lot number. Solicitation # 36E79727R0007 will be electronically issued in commercial item format in accordance with FAR Part 12 on or about December 18, 2026, with a tentative closing date of January 7, 2027. The NAICS code for this procurement is 325412. Any future amendments and other miscellaneous documents will be available electronically for download at SAM.gov. No paper copies of the solicitation will be available, and no telephone requests for paper copies of the solicitation will be accepted. Interested offerors are advised to continuously check Contracting Opportunities at SAM.gov for any changes to this solicitation. All responsible sources may submit an offer that if timely received, will be considered. The point of contact for this procurement is James Sullivan. title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including:1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery.2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material.3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting.4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS).5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. title: ND NP THRO 204(1) Buck Hill Road
description: INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION WITH HUBZONE PREFERENCE PROJECT NUMBER: ND NP THRO 204(1) PROJECT NAME: Buck Hill Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Buck Hill Road, also known as Route 204, is located in Billings County within Theodore Roosevelt (THRO) National Park (NP) in the southeast portion of the park near the South Unit, Medora, ND. The route is located in mountainous terrain at approximate elevation of 2,500 to 2,800 feet. It begins at the intersection of Buck Hill Road and South Unit Scenic Loop Road. The route then proceeds southeasterly for approximately � of a mile and ascends approximately 300 feet vertically to the Buck Hill Overlook parking area. The route is located entirely within Theodore Roosevelt NP. There is one (1) base schedule and no options. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project includes three major components; 1) Approximately � mile of roadway rehabilitation, 2) Approximately 1,000 linear feet of deep subexcavation to address an existing landslide, and 3) Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot. The main roadway rehabilitation includes pulverization of the existing roadway, placement of new roadway aggregate, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement and replacing existing guardrail with new guardrail. Additionally, this work includes constructing new paved ditches and installing concrete curb and gutter along most of the length of the roadway. This includes installation of several drainage inlets and culverts as well as new striping and signage. The deep subexcavation work includes removal of approximately existing unsuitable material to a 10 feet depth for a continuous 1,000 linear foot length of roadway and replacing with suitable material with geosynthetic reinforcement and installing subsurface drainage. A geotechnical report will be provided with the PS&E package. Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot expands and adds more parking spaces and accommodates larger trucks, recreational vehicles, and tour buses. The work includes removing the existing pavement, placing embankment material, new aggregate base, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement. This work also includes constructing accessible parking, placing new concrete sidewalk and curb and gutter, and striping and signage. New trash receptacles and stone benches will be installed as part of the new parking area. Buck Hill Road may be closed for the duration of construction. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: Approximate quantities for major work items: 11,000 cubic yards of subexcavation 1,000 linear feet of geocomposite sheet drain 2,000 tons of hot asphalt concrete pavement 5,000 tons of roadway aggregate 550 linear feet of 24-inch pipe culvert (thick walled HDPE, fused) 5,100 linear feet of concrete curb and gutter (tan and onyx colored) 650 square yards of concrete sidewalk (tan colored) 1,600 linear feet of guardrail ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � October 2026 Award - January 2027 Construction � April 2027 through November 2027 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000

description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) / Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) / National Disaster and Emergency Management University (NDEMU) intends to negotiate on a sole source basis (IAW RFO FAR 12) with American Council on Education (ACE), One Dupont Circle NW, Washington, DC 20036, as the only responsible source that capable of providing comprehensive higher-education curriculum review, academic quality assurance, and college credit evaluation services for NDEMU�s residential, virtual, and distance-learning course offerings. Market evaluation confirmed that American Council on Education (ACE) Learning Evaluations remains uniquely positioned as the sole established industry standard for evaluating non-formal workplace training and assigning standardized college credit recommendations. ACE recommendations are recognized and integrated across both federal agencies and post-secondary higher education institutions. Furthermore, ACE provides an integrated ecosystem including entry in the ACE National Guide, direct learner transcript advocacy, and automated digital badge issuance via Credly, which independent regional or institutional accreditors do not offer for non-collegiate course providers. Therefore, ACE is the only source that can provide comprehensive higher-education curriculum review, academic quality assurance, and college credit evaluation services for NDEMU�s residential, virtual, and distance-learning course offerings. This acquisition is being conducted under simplified acquisition procedures (IAW RFO FAR 12). The intended procurement will be classified under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 611710-Educational Support Services with a Small Business Size Standard of $24M. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. However, parties interested in responding to this notice will need to submit technical data, sufficient to determine capability in providing the same product. title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. title: ND NP THRO 204(1) Buck Hill Road
description: INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION WITH HUBZONE PREFERENCE PROJECT NUMBER: ND NP THRO 204(1) PROJECT NAME: Buck Hill Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Buck Hill Road, also known as Route 204, is located in Billings County within Theodore Roosevelt (THRO) National Park (NP) in the southeast portion of the park near the South Unit, Medora, ND. The route is located in mountainous terrain at approximate elevation of 2,500 to 2,800 feet. It begins at the intersection of Buck Hill Road and South Unit Scenic Loop Road. The route then proceeds southeasterly for approximately � of a mile and ascends approximately 300 feet vertically to the Buck Hill Overlook parking area. The route is located entirely within Theodore Roosevelt NP. There is one (1) base schedule and no options. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project includes three major components; 1) Approximately � mile of roadway rehabilitation, 2) Approximately 1,000 linear feet of deep subexcavation to address an existing landslide, and 3) Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot. The main roadway rehabilitation includes pulverization of the existing roadway, placement of new roadway aggregate, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement and replacing existing guardrail with new guardrail. Additionally, this work includes constructing new paved ditches and installing concrete curb and gutter along most of the length of the roadway. This includes installation of several drainage inlets and culverts as well as new striping and signage. The deep subexcavation work includes removal of approximately existing unsuitable material to a 10 feet depth for a continuous 1,000 linear foot length of roadway and replacing with suitable material with geosynthetic reinforcement and installing subsurface drainage. A geotechnical report will be provided with the PS&E package. Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot expands and adds more parking spaces and accommodates larger trucks, recreational vehicles, and tour buses. The work includes removing the existing pavement, placing embankment material, new aggregate base, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement. This work also includes constructing accessible parking, placing new concrete sidewalk and curb and gutter, and striping and signage. New trash receptacles and stone benches will be installed as part of the new parking area. Buck Hill Road may be closed for the duration of construction. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: Approximate quantities for major work items: 11,000 cubic yards of subexcavation 1,000 linear feet of geocomposite sheet drain 2,000 tons of hot asphalt concrete pavement 5,000 tons of roadway aggregate 550 linear feet of 24-inch pipe culvert (thick walled HDPE, fused) 5,100 linear feet of concrete curb and gutter (tan and onyx colored) 650 square yards of concrete sidewalk (tan colored) 1,600 linear feet of guardrail ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � October 2026 Award - January 2027 Construction � April 2027 through November 2027 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000

This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including:1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery.2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material.3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting.4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS).5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. Please review and submit any questions related to this solicitation through the PIEE module link found down in the attachments section by October 19th. These questions and answers will be public. QandA will be closed after October 19th. Proposals shall be submitted through the solicitation module in PIEE. See the PIEE submittal instructions for directions on submitting proposal documents in PIEE. Any extensions to this solicitation will be posted here. Solicitation FA822427R0002 was amended to correct the due date to be Nov 3rd, 2026 by 3:00PM Mountain Time. Please refer to solicitation FA822427R00020001. No other changes were made from the original version. Q and A V1 posted on 9 Oct with updated questions and answers from industry. Amendment 002 posted on 9 Oct see Solicitation amendment 002 for details.

title: TX FW LGA 10(5) Steve Thompson Wildlife Drive
description: PROJECT NUMBER: TX FW LGA 10(5) PROJECT NAME: Steve Thompson Wildlife Drive PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The proposed project is in Laguna Atascosa National Wildlife Refuge in Cameron County, Texas approximately 25 miles east of Harlingen, Texas. The existing terrain is flat. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The proposed project includes full depth reclamation of existing driving surface which includes chip seal material, and existing gravel. After completing full-depth reclamation new aggregate surface course will be added to create a driving surface that has a consistent width. The project also includes installation of aluminum gate and a small concrete pad and safety improvement signs and speed bumps. The project includes three (3) alternate bid items for Aggregate Surface Course (TON) with one (1) being awarded. Alternate 1: 2-inches of aggregate surface course added to Bayside Drive and Steve Thompson Wildlife Drive and terminating at Renee�s Overlook Parking Area. Alternate 2: 2-inches of aggregate surface course added to Bayside Drive and Steve Thompson Wildlife Drive. Alternate 3: 3-inches of aggregate surface course added to Bayside Drive and Steve Thompson Wildlife Drive and terminating at Renee�s Overlook Parking Area.

title: Borough of Millvale, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: This is a Presolicitation Notice only. This is not a Solicitation (Request for Quote). No purchase order will be awarded from this announcement. Any applicable attachments for this project (i.e., Drawings and Specifications) will be issued at the time of the Solicitation. This procurement is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. All interested and capable small business offerors are encouraged to submit a quote. Project Description The Millvale LPP was constructed by U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) in 1980 under the authority of Section 205 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 as amended. The project consists of about 6,200 feet of channel improvement including concrete gravity retaining walls, concrete wall supports, anchored concrete toe blocks, concrete cap walls, stone-filled gabion mattresses, flap gates and access ramps. The LPP is an urban Flood Control Work (FCW), and it is not a multipurpose project. Heavy rains from 1-12 April 2024 caused flooding which damaged the Project within Girty�s Run, including bank erosion, shoaling, erosion of the improved channel, ruptured gabion baskets, washed-out concrete buttresses, and erosion of grouted riprap. Of particular concern are the washed-out buttresses which have migrated to the center of the improved channel, impeding streamflow. If the buttresses are not removed and stream bank improvements continue to deteriorate, there is a risk that debris will continue to accumulate and could ultimately damage the channel downstream of the impediment. To address these damages, Allegheny County requested rehabilitation assistance from USACE through the PL 84-99 program, which authorizes USACE to rehabilitate eligible Federal and non-Federal LPPs damaged or destroyed by floods. An agreement was signed on 6 August 2025 between the Borough of Millvale and USACE to complete the necessary repairs. Some of the major features of work are, but not limited to: Temporary Stream Diversion, Dewatering, and Environmental Controls Stream Flow Control: Design, furnish, operate, maintain, and remove a temporary stream diversion and bypass pumping system to perform all channel bottom and bank work in a dry, dewatered state. Effluent Filtration: Discharge from pumping systems must pass through approved sediment and debris control filtration before re-entering Girty's Run. E&S Controls: Install, inspect, and maintain erosion and sediment controls compliant with PADEP Publication 363-2134-008. The project is located along Girty�s Run and Boomer Run between Station 68+00 and Station 73+80, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $300,000.00 and $350,000.00. The contractor is responsible for all project submittals, including a Quality Control Plan, Accident Prevention Plan, and various shop drawings and product data for government approval. Special Notice: Safety and Qualification Requirements Safety Compliance (EM 385-1-1): Offerors are advised that all work on this project must strictly comply with the latest edition of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1) (Link: https://www.publications.usace.army.mil/Portals/76/EM%20385-1-1%20_EFFECTIVE%2015March2024.pdf). Prior to commencing work, the contractor must submit and secure Government approval for a site-specific Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and comprehensive Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs). To enforce these standards, the contractor must employ a full-time, dedicated Level 1 Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO) who must be present on-site at all times when work is in progress. The SSHO may also serve as the Quality Control System Manager (QCSM) but is strictly prohibited from serving as the project Superintendent. See Personnel and Contractor Qualifications. Personnel and Contractor Qualifications: To ensure technical competency and safe execution of this project, the Government requires key personnel to meet strict experience thresholds. The contractor must assign a Project Superintendent with a minimum of five (5) years of construction experience, with at least five (5) of those years acting as a superintendent on earthwork and channel restoration projects similar in size and complexity. Additionally, the contractor must provide a Quality Control System Manager (QCSM) who has a minimum of five (5) years of construction experience on similar projects and holds a valid "Construction Quality Management for Contractors" (CQM-C) certification, as well as a dedicated Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO). General Information The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The solicitation will be issued on or about 4 November 2026, via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov. The anticipated award date is 30 November 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Basis of Award is best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO 12.203(a) and RFO 13.202, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that are unrealistically low or exceed available funds for this requirement. Small Business Contractors are advised that APEX Accelerators provide free, expert assistance to small businesses interested in competing for federal, state, and local government contracts. Small businesses are strongly encouraged to connect with their local APEX Accelerators to leverage these valuable services. The APEX Accelerators Website is: https://www.apexaccelerators.us/#/. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/ then scrolling down on right hand side of page by clicking on �View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here�. To submit a quote for this project, your company must: 1) Be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) and maintain an active registration status. 2) be registered in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) for the Solicitation Module with the PROPOSAL MANAGER Role. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration Registering in SAM.gov includes both entity validation and entity registration. To register in SAM: a) Navigate to SAM.gov b) Select Sign-In (top right) c) Select Create an Account then follow the instructions d) After Account is set-up, Select Sign-In e) Under the Entity Management widget, select �Get Started� button f) Select Register Entity. As part of the entity registration, a Unique Entity ID will be assigned. For additional information on SAM To Register your Entity (Company), please visit https:/www.fsd.gov/gsafsd_sp?id=gsa_index. Here you will find the following: Get Started with your Registration Check Registration Status � ACTIVE, INACTIVE, PENDING Update your Registration Become an Entity Administrator Validate your Entity *Access User Guides *By selecting this option, you can obtain a Quick Start Guide for Contract Registrations. Also, here you will find in addition to the User Guides - FAQs, Videos, and Definitions. PLEASE NOTE: It is mandatory that all companies be registered in SAM in order to receive federal contracts. There is no charge to register or maintain your company (entity) registration. Login.gov manages usernames and passwords for SAM.gov. *Important* Registration Information Registration can take at least ten (10) business days to be active in SAM.gov. Registration must be in active status upon offer submission

title: Germany – Sanitary fixture installation work – Modernisierung GS Dorschbergschule - Installation von Sanitäreinrichtungen und Installation und Verlegung von Abwasserleitungen
description: Die Grundschule Dorschberg in Wörth a. Rh. wurde 1966 baulich errichtet und liegt hinter dem Mittelbau der Carl–Benz–Gesamtschule in Wörth am Rhein. Die Grundschule besteht aus vier Gebäudeteilen, zu welchen ein ein- bzw. zweigeschossiger Gebäudeteil mit Verbindungsgängen gehört sowie eine Pausenhalle mit einem Verwaltungstrakt und einem eingeschossigen Pavillonbau mit vier Pavillongebäuden. Die Gebäude sind mit Pausengängen verbunden und verfügen über zwei Toilettengebäude. Die ein- bis zweigeschossigen Gebäude wurden in massiver Bauweise mit Beton-Fertigteilen errichtet und weisen Flachdächer in unterschiedlichen Höhenlagen mit umlaufender Attika auf und wurden bis heute mehrfach saniert und modernisiert. Mitte der 1990er Jahre fand eine Betonsanierung statt. In diesem Zuge wurde ein Wärmedämm-Verbundsystem und die Alucobond-Verkleidungen der Attiken und der Fertigteilstützen angebracht. Wesentliche bauliche Maßnahmen - Der bestehende eingeschossige Klassentrakt wird aufgestockt und der bisherige Innenhofbereich zwischen den beiden bestehenden Klassentrakten wird geschlossen und überdacht. Hierzu wird die nicht ausreichend tragfähige Spannbetondecke über dem nördlichen Klassentakt zurück gebaut und durch eine neue Stahlbeton-Massivdecke ersetzt. - Das neue Obergeschoss wird in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise mit tragenden Wänden als Massivholzkonstruktion bzw. Holzständerkonstruktion und oberster Geschossdecke als Brettsperrholzkonstruktion errichtet. - Die zentrale Aula wird mit einer Glasdachkonstruktion versehen. - Die Spannbetondecke im Flurbereich über dem bestehenden Kriechkeller des Nordtraktes muss durch Stahlträger ertüchtigt werden. - Kleinteilige Grundrissänderungen im Bestand - Die Pavillons werden entkernt und zur erweiterten überdachten Pausenhoffläche - Verbesserung des Wärmeschutzes sämtlicher Gebäudehüllflächen (Dachflächen, Fenster, hinterlüftete Holzfassaden, Kellerdeckendämmung) - Modernisierung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung inkl. kontrollierten Lüftungseinrichtung mit Wärmerückgewinnung, energiesparender Beleuchtungssysteme, Gebäudeautomation, einschließlich der digitalen Anforderungen an Schulgebäude - Optimierung des Brandschutzes und Umsetzung des schulischen Schutzkonzepts

title: Germany – Structural shell work – Stadt Drolshagen - Bauliche Erweiterung der Gräfin-Sayn-Verbundgrundschule zum Ausbau der Ganztagsbetreuung am Hauptstandort Drolshagen | Rohbauarbeiten 1. Bauabschnitt
description: Für die Bestandsgebäude der Gräfin-Sayn-Schule in Drolshagen besteht ein baulicher, funktionaler sowie teilweise energetischer Sanierungsbedarf. Zudem ist eine Anpassung an aktuelle pädagogische Anforderungen sowie an moderne Nutzungs- und Raumkonzepte vorgesehen. Im Zuge der geplanten Maßnahmen werden Umbau-, Modernisierungs-, Sanierungs- sowie Teilabbruch- und Erweiterungsmaßnahmen erforderlich. Die Liegenschaftsadresse lautet: Gräfin-Sayn-Schule Am Buscheid 2 57489 Drolshagen Gebäudebeschreibung: Die bestehende Schulanlage der Gräfin-Sayn-Schule besteht aus mehreren miteinander verbundenen bzw. separaten Gebäudeteilen unterschiedlicher Baujahre. Die Gebäude umfassen: • Unterrichts- und Klassenräume • Verwaltungs- und Nebenräume • Sanitärbereiche • Fachräume sowie ergänzende Nutzflächen Die Gebäude sind teilweise mehrgeschossig ausgeführt und über befestigte Schulhofflächen sowie interne Wege miteinander verbunden. Die Außenanlagen bestehen überwiegend aus: • asphaltierten Schulhofflächen • befestigten Zugangs- und Verkehrsflächen • Grün- und Aufenthaltsbereichen Neues Nutzungskonzept: Im Rahmen der geplanten Baumaßnahme wird die bestehende Schulanlage abschnittsweise weiterentwickelt und modernisiert. Die Maßnahmen umfassen insbesondere: • Teilabbruch einzelner Gebäudebereiche, die den heutigen Anforderungen nicht mehr entsprechen • Sanierung und Modernisierung von Bestandsgebäuden, insbesondere im Hinblick auf: • energetische Verbesserung (Dach, Fassade, Fenster) • funktionale Anpassung der Grundrisse • brandschutztechnische Ertüchtigung • Umbauarbeiten im Innenbereich zur Anpassung an das aktuelle Raumprogramm • Ergänzende Neubau- bzw. Erweiterungsmaßnahmen Die Bauausführung erfolgt in mehreren Bauabschnitten, um den Schulbetrieb aufrechtzuerhalten. Die auszuschreibende Leistung betrifft die Rohbauarbeiten für den 1. Bauabschnitt.

Hankinnan kilpailutus on hankintalain (Laki julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeussopimuksista (1397/2016) mukainen EU kynnysarvon ylittävä tavarahankinta. Kaikki muut tarkemmat ja yksityiskohtaisemmat tiedot on kuvattu tässä tarjouspyynnössä sekä muussa tarjouspyyntöaineistossa. Hankinnassa noudatetaan NLM10- ehtoja. Hankinnan sopimuskauden ja sopimuskauden aikaisen työkokonaisuuden valvojana toimii Kainuun hyvinvointialueen sähkönsinööri, Ismo Tolonen (ismo.tolonen@kainuu.fi). title: NGC
description: The Modernization Branch of the F-22 Division (AFLCMC/WAR) is exploring the market for qualified firms to provide next-generation hydrogenated, dielectric cooling fluid. The material shall consist of a synthetic, hydrocarbon base oil with suitable additives as needed. This Sources Sought/RFI is looking for information on improved heat transfer capability. While calculating exact forced convection heat transfer requires parameters outside of fluid properties (e.g. velocity, pipe diameter, etc.), the F-22 Division seeks to improve one or more fluid properties that correlate to improved heat transfer capability. Current coolant density, thermal conductivity, specific heat values, and coefficient of thermal expansion are listed within the attachment to this RFI.

title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. Please review and submit any questions related to this solicitation through the PIEE module link found down in the attachments section by October 19th. These questions and answers will be public. Q&A will be closed after October 19th. Proposals shall be submitted through the solicitation module in PIEE. See the PIEE submittal instructions for directions on submitting proposal documents in PIEE. Any extensions to this solicitation will be posted here. title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded.
